_doc: HMTc Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) compiler config. Method v2.0, consumer-chemical form. Household cleaning products are LARGELY UNREGULATED for heavy-metal content: the eco-label / disclosure regimes in the taxonomy's regulatory anchors (EPA Safer Choice, Green Seal GS-8, CA SB 258, NY Household Cleaner Disclosure Act) are ingredient-DISCLOSURE and eco-labeling regimes, NOT heavy-metal maximum-level limits. The ONE credible sovereign that directly sets heavy-metal limits on the product class is China GB 14930.1-2022 (National food safety standard - Detergents), which governs detergents that clean food, tableware, and food-contact articles: a species-specific total-arsenic limit (Type A 3.0 / Type B 5.0 mg/kg) plus a grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb). Because most cells have no sovereign ML, they resolve to read-across (nearest applicable consumer-chemical sovereign), control (published analytical method + escalation rule, no number), or not-material (rebuttable, evidence-tested). NO cell is an occurrence-derived percentile; the cleaning-product occurrence corpus (zhang2010 dish soap ten-metal panel; ecetoc1992 Ni/Cr/Cr-VI in dish/all-purpose/specialty cleaners; abulude2007; torres2024) is used ONLY to substantiate not-material claims and confirm which metals are materially present (Pb, Cd, Ni, Cr, Cr-VI are present -> read-across or control, never not-material), never to set a number. NATIVE BASIS is total heavy-metal content in the product as placed on the market (mg/kg of product) for EVERY subcategory: it is GB 14930.1's own basis and the only basis in which a rinse-off/wipe cleaning product can actually be tested. Food-contact-migration limits (EU 10/2011) are a DIFFERENT basis (migration into food from a permanent article) that does not apply to a rinse-off product and would produce indefensible (100-1000x over-strict) numbers if conflated onto a total-content basis; they are cited only as the exposure-pathway rationale for the dish-contacting rows, never as a numeric ceiling. BASIS IS NEVER CONFLATED across a min(): the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling is a grouped-basis sovereign limit carried inline (like the Cat-9 nickel-release limit that does not fit the register's ug/kg species schema) and applied as a conservative per-species bound to Pb/Cd/tHg, not min()'d against species-specific read-across values in a different basis. Three exposure sub-pathways: (A) food-contact-cleaning (dish soaps, automatic-dishwasher detergents, rinse aids -> residue-on-dishes ingestion, GB 14930.1 governs); (B) hard-surface / incidental-dermal (all other cleaners -> cosmetics/personal-care read-across is the nearer analog); (C) FIFRA antimicrobial (disinfectants/sanitizers -> EPA-registered pesticides, a distinct testing bucket; organotin screened per REACH entry 20). See docs/governance/category-12-step0-lock.md.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, consumer-chemical form; native basis = total heavy-metal content in product as placed on market, mg/kg; no cross-basis min)

read_across_regime.note: The nearest applicable coherent SOVEREIGN regime for the incidental-dermal pathway is China's mandatory national cosmetic trace-metal standard (Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics, 2015; NMPA). It is statutory, comprehensive across the toxic panel (Pb/tAs/Cd/tHg), and CONSERVATIVE relative to actual cleaning-product exposure (a cosmetic is prolonged leave-on skin contact; a hard-surface cleaner is incidental dermal). A single coherent regime is read across rather than cherry-picking the strictest number per analyte across regimes, which would build an element-wise-max envelope no sovereign enforces (the anti-pattern the methodology forbids). Stricter guidance values exist (Germany BfR: Pb 2.0, Cd 0.1, tHg 0.1, tAs 0.5 mg/kg) but are guidance, not statutory maxima, and are logged as precautionary-ratchet candidates for a future edition, not adopted as the government-limit-default baseline.

food-contact-cleaning.governing_basis: GB 14930.1-2022 (China; National food safety standard - Detergents), Type B: detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging, and containers. Total arsenic binds the GB 14930.1 Type B species-specific ceiling; Pb, Cd, and tHg are bounded by GB 14930.1's grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg sum). Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.
food-contact-cleaning.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content in product as placed on the market (mg/kg product)

grouped.basis_label: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
grouped.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb, sum of heavy metals). Lead is a member of the summed group, so it is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; a conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

regulatory_alignment.basis_label: total arsenic, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
regulatory_alignment.label: GB 14930.1-2022 Type B total-arsenic ceiling for detergents used on tableware and food-contact articles (5.0 mg/kg). The stricter Type A ceiling (3.0 mg/kg) governs detergents applied directly to food (washing produce), a different use, and is a same-instrument scope sibling, not a missed stricter limit.

not_material.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for detergents or cleaning products; GB 14930.1 and every consumer-chemical trace-metal instrument regulate TOTAL arsenic (see the tAs cell), which bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). Inorganic arsenic is a dietary/water speciation with no separate cleaning-product instrument. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated inorganic arsenic in these products.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling (GB 14930.1 Type B, 5.0 mg/kg); no inorganic-arsenic limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR
not_material.cross_sourced: parent tAs published (GB 14930.1 Type B) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no iAs cleaning-product limit); occurrence corpus (zhang2010; ecetoc1992) measured no arsenic speciation
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation only if total arsenic approaches the ceiling.

grouped.basis_label: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
grouped.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb). Cadmium is a member of the summed group and is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

grouped.basis_label: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
grouped.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb). Mercury is a member of the summed group and is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation or migration pathway in a detergent formulation; it is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation. Every mercury instrument that touches this product class regulates total mercury (GB 14930.1's grouped heavy-metals ceiling, see the tHg cell), which bounds any organomercury fraction. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated methylmercury in these products.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-mercury (grouped heavy-metals) ceiling (GB 14930.1, <=1.0 mg/kg as Pb); no methylmercury limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR

not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by CV-AAS or ICP-MS; no reflex methylmercury speciation defined for cleaning products (no formation pathway).

control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market (acid digestion).
control.escalation_rule: Nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitizer and is measured in household cleaning products (zhang2010 dish soap; ecetoc1992 dish/all-purpose/specialty cleaners). No jurisdiction sets a numeric total-nickel maximum for cleaning products, so certification screens total nickel and escalates a lot above the running category control band to ALARA review rather than pass/failing on an invented number.
control.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis. A drinking-water or article-migration nickel value is a different basis and is not read across.

control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
control.escalation_rule: Aluminium is Tier-2 (low toxicity by the oral/dermal routes at cleaning-product exposure) and may be a functional mineral ingredient (alumina abrasives, aluminosilicate builders). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product aluminium maximum. Screen total aluminium; a lot outside the functional-ingredient expectation triggers ingredient review.
control.rationale: No sovereign ML; potential functional-ingredient source means a not-material claim would be false. Screen, do not publish a number.

control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
control.escalation_rule: Total chromium is measured in cleaning products (zhang2010; ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product chromium maximum. Screen total chromium and reflex Cr(VI) speciation where total chromium is elevated or the formulation is oxidizing/acidic.
control.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis.

control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by IC-ICP-MS with alkaline extraction (US EPA 3060A / 7199) on oxidizing or acidic formulations.
control.escalation_rule: Cr(VI) is measured in some consumer cleaning products (ecetoc1992) and oxidizing/acidic chemistries can stabilize it. No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product Cr(VI) maximum. Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on oxidizing/acidic formulations and where total chromium is elevated; escalate a positive Cr(VI) result to ALARA review.
control.rationale: Measured in the corpus; a real hazard on oxidizing chemistries; no sovereign number, so a method + escalation rule is published rather than an invented threshold.

not_material.rationale: Inorganic tin has no source in a detergent/dish-cleaning formulation (no tinplate or canned-food pathway). Organotin is a DISTINCT species (biocide/stabiliser) restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 and is screened separately where a formulation could carry it; it does not bound, and is not bounded by, this inorganic-tin cell. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-tin limit for cleaning products, and no routed occurrence source measured tin (the zhang2010 ten-metal panel excludes tin).

not_material.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII (entry 20 organotin); US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada

not_material.reference_method: Periodic ICP-MS inorganic-tin verification; organotin (DBT/DOT/TBT as Sn) screened separately by GC-ICP-MS where a biocidal-organotin pathway is plausible.

hard-surface-dermal.governing_basis: No sovereign sets heavy-metal maximums for hard-surface / incidental-dermal cleaning products; the eco-label and disclosure regimes (EPA Safer Choice, Green Seal GS-8, CA SB 258, NY Household Cleaner Disclosure Act) are ingredient-disclosure and eco-labeling regimes, not heavy-metal MLs. The toxic panel (Pb/tAs/Cd/tHg) is read across from the nearest applicable coherent sovereign regime (China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic trace-metal limits), conservative because a cosmetic is prolonged leave-on skin contact and a hard-surface cleaner is incidental dermal. Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.

fifra-antimicrobial.governing_basis: EPA-registered antimicrobial products (US FIFRA) are a distinct testing bucket. The FIFRA Confidential Statement of Formula and the antimicrobial active ingredient govern registration; any metal-based active (e.g., silver, copper) is a DECLARED ACTIVE, not a contaminant, and is outside the HMTc contaminant panel. No FIFRA or FDA sanitizing-solution instrument sets a heavy-metal contaminant maximum for the product. Heavy-metal contaminants take the consumer-chemical read-across (NMPA 2015); organotin is screened per REACH entry 20 given the historical organotin-biocide pathway. Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.
fifra-antimicrobial.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content in product as placed on the market (mg/kg product)

all-purpose-cleaners.name: All-purpose cleaners
all-purpose-cleaners.scope_note: Multi-surface household cleaners for general hard surfaces. Incidental-dermal exposure; nickel and chromium are measured in this class (ecetoc1992) and screened.

kitchen-countertop-cleaners.name: Kitchen/countertop cleaners
kitchen-countertop-cleaners.scope_note: Cleaners for kitchen and food-preparation surfaces. Food-preparation surfaces create a food-residue-transfer (ingestion) sub-pathway; GB 14930.1 Type B (food-contact-equipment cleaning) is a relevant conservative reference for that sub-pathway, but the binding basis is total content in the product as placed on the market with a cosmetics/personal-care read-across for the primary incidental-dermal pathway.

bathroom-tub-tile-cleaners.name: Bathroom/tub/tile cleaners
bathroom-tub-tile-cleaners.scope_note: Cleaners for tubs, tiles, and bathroom surfaces. Often acidic or oxidizing; Cr(VI) reflex speciation applies to oxidizing/acidic formulations.

toilet-bowl-cleaners.name: Toilet bowl cleaners
toilet-bowl-cleaners.scope_note: Acidic or oxidizing (hypochlorite/acid) toilet-bowl cleaners. Cr(VI) reflex speciation applies to the oxidizing/acidic chemistry.

window-glass-mirror-cleaners.name: Window/glass/mirror cleaners
window-glass-mirror-cleaners.scope_note: Glass and mirror cleaners (typically dilute surfactant/solvent sprays).

floor-cleaners-hard-surface.name: Floor cleaners (hard surface)
floor-cleaners-hard-surface.scope_note: Hard-surface floor cleaners (dilutable concentrates and ready-to-use).

floor-finishes-strippers.name: Floor finishes & strippers
floor-finishes-strippers.scope_note: Floor finishes and finish strippers (strongly alkaline or solvent-based). Basis remains total content in the product as placed on the market.

carpet-cleaners.name: Carpet cleaners
carpet-cleaners.scope_note: Carpet shampoos and extraction cleaners (rinse/extract off; incidental-dermal exposure).

carpet-spot-removers.name: Carpet spot removers
carpet-spot-removers.scope_note: Spot and stain removers for carpet (spot-applied; incidental-dermal exposure).

degreasers.name: Degreasers
degreasers.scope_note: Heavy-duty degreasers (alkaline or solvent). Incidental-dermal exposure.

oven-grill-bbq-cleaners.name: Oven/grill/BBQ cleaners
oven-grill-bbq-cleaners.scope_note: Strongly alkaline / oxidizing oven, grill, and BBQ cleaners. Cr(VI) reflex speciation applies to the oxidizing/caustic chemistry. Applied to cooking surfaces but rinsed before food contact; treated as incidental-dermal with a total-content basis.

appliance-cleaners.name: Appliance cleaners (including stainless steel cleaners)
appliance-cleaners.scope_note: Appliance and stainless-steel cleaners (may contain oxalic or other acids). Incidental-dermal exposure.

descalers.name: Descalers
descalers.scope_note: Acidic descalers (citric, lactic, sulfamic, phosphoric). Cr(VI) reflex speciation applies to the acidic chemistry.

dish-soaps-manual.name: Dish soaps (manual dishwashing)
dish-soaps-manual.scope_note: Manual dishwashing liquids and soaps that clean tableware and food-contact utensils. GB 14930.1 Type B (detergents for tableware and food-contact tools) directly governs the product class; total arsenic binds the Type B ceiling and Pb/Cd/tHg are bounded by the grouped heavy-metals ceiling. Nickel and chromium are measured in this class (zhang2010; ecetoc1992) and screened.

automatic-dishwasher-detergents.name: Automatic dishwasher detergents
automatic-dishwasher-detergents.scope_note: Machine dishwashing detergents (powder, gel, tablets, pods) that clean tableware in an automatic dishwasher. GB 14930.1 Type B (food-contact-article cleaning) governs the product class.

rinse-aids.name: Rinse aids
rinse-aids.scope_note: Automatic-dishwasher rinse aids that contact tableware during the rinse cycle. GB 14930.1 Type B (food-contact-article cleaning) governs the product class.

cleaning-wipes-household.name: Cleaning wipes (household surface wipes)
cleaning-wipes-household.scope_note: Pre-moistened household surface wipes. When used on food-preparation surfaces they create a food-residue-transfer sub-pathway (GB 14930.1 Type B is a relevant conservative reference), but the binding basis is total content of the wipe liquor as placed on the market with a cosmetics/personal-care read-across for the primary incidental-dermal pathway. Non-woven substrate metals are a separate textile question outside the product-liquor content scope.

drain-maintainers-cleaners.name: Drain maintainers/cleaners (including biological-based)
drain-maintainers-cleaners.scope_note: Drain openers, maintainers, and enzymatic/biological drain products (caustic, oxidizing, or enzyme-based). Minimal direct human contact; total-content basis retained.

odor-removers-hard-surfaces.name: Odor removers for hard surfaces
odor-removers-hard-surfaces.scope_note: Hard-surface odor eliminators and neutralizers (sprays). Incidental-dermal exposure.

household-specialty-cleaners-other.name: Other household specialty cleaners (by functional use-case)
household-specialty-cleaners-other.scope_note: Residual bucket for household specialty cleaners not covered by a named row (by functional use-case). Nickel, chromium, and Cr(VI) are measured in this class (ecetoc1992) and screened. Products that clean food-contact articles route to the food-contact-cleaning rows; fabric-intended products route to Category 19.

disinfectants-sanitizers.name: Disinfectants and sanitizers (EPA-registered antimicrobial sprays, wipes, concentrates)
disinfectants-sanitizers.scope_note: EPA-registered antimicrobial products under FIFRA (sprays, wipes, concentrates) - a distinct testing bucket. Metal-based actives (silver, copper) are declared actives, not contaminants, and are outside the HMTc contaminant panel. Organotin is screened per REACH entry 20 given the historical organotin-biocide pathway. No FIFRA/FDA instrument sets a heavy-metal contaminant maximum for the product.
